preamble: The voiceless postalveolar fricative [ʃ] becomes the palatal glide [j] before a stop. The clearest case is Western Samic, where vocalization of Proto-Samic *š to *j before a stop is one of the shared Western innovations (not in Sea Sámi), while the Eastern Samic languages keep the sibilant: Proto-Samic *kuoškë 'rapids' > Northern Sami guoika but Inari Sami kuošˈkâ.
